items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: my first 78 was Duke Ellington on two sides. “Tootin’ Through the Roof” was one of the tunes

ctx.x: I think it’s also Ted Nash.

Yes, right. I think the one I listened to was his uncle or granddad. But anyhow I listened to him a lot and I had a quartet record from the Westlake School of Music out in California with a tenor, piano, bass and drums. And I don’t know whatever happened to them but I played that over and over. I had an Oscar Peterson — excuse me — Oscar Pettiford record that I bought, and then I bought — my first LP — my first 78 was Duke Ellington on two sides. “Tootin’ Through the Roof” was one of the tunes and I forget what…

Wayne Shorter and Michael Brecker, etcetera, etcetera. But in the early stages I listened to all those people. And I also listened to trios, piano trios, bass players. I’ve probably got twelve, thirteen thousand LPs, maybe more than that.
